messages.subject: PyStan: Value error in misc.py
parts:
Hi,

I am using PyStan to fit a model to auction data. I get a value error for variable __header__ in pystan/misc.py
Any hints what can be causing this error?
Below are the error message as well as the model code.

INFO:pystan:COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6 NOW.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "ovr_stan.py", line 76, in <module>
    iter=1000, chains=4)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/api.py", line 385, in stan
    n_jobs=n_jobs, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/model.py", line 685, in sampling
    fit = self.fit_class(data)
  File "stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.pyx", line 426, in stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.StanFit4Model.__cinit__ (/tmp/tmpsuFrsU/pystan/stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.cpp:7834)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/misc.py", line 366, in _split_data
    raise ValueError(msg.format(k))
ValueError: Variable __header__ is neither int nor float nor list/array thereof


ovr_code = """
functions{
    real revenue(real y, real B, real b) {
        real rev;
        rev <- if_else(y>b, y, b);
        rev <- if_else(B>y, 0, rev);
        return rev;
    }
}
data {
    int<lower=0> N;                            // number of observations
    int<lower=1> d;                            // number of dimensions
    matrix[N,d] x;                               // covariates
    vector[N] B;                                 // highest bid
    vector[N] b;                                  // second bid
    int<lower=0,upper=1> z[N];            // hallucinated data
}
parameters {
    real w0;                // intercept
    vector[d] w;            // weight vector
    real<lower=0> sigma;    // std
    vector[N] y;            // reserve price

}
model {
    y ~ normal(w0 + x*w, sigma);
    for (i in 1:N)
     z[i] ~ bernoulli(exp(-revenue(y[i],B[i],b[i])));
}
"""

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan: Value error in misc.py
parts:
Hi, Maja & welcome to the Stan list.

I can't help you with the PyStan, but you're the
second person to ask about this Auction model --- sounds
like it's part of the PPAML task.

But I can comment on the model itself --- see below.

> On Apr 6, 2015, at 11:58 AM, Maja Rudolph <marir...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I am using PyStan to fit a model to auction data. I get a value error for variable __header__ in pystan/misc.py
> Any hints what can be causing this error?
> Below are the error message as well as the model code.
>
> INFO:pystan:COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6 NOW.
> Traceback (most recent call last):
> File "ovr_stan.py", line 76, in <module>
> iter=1000, chains=4)
> File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/api.py", line 385, in stan
> n_jobs=n_jobs, **kwargs)
> File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/model.py", line 685, in sampling
> fit = self.fit_class(data)
> File "stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.pyx", line 426, in stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.StanFit4Model.__cinit__ (/tmp/tmpsuFrsU/pystan/stanfit4anon_model_07b8cf1021ff43e6843005b4d44744e6_996311c807219e4458bfdda0257145f8.cpp:7834)
> File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/pystan/misc.py", line 366, in _split_data
> raise ValueError(msg.format(k))
> ValueError: Variable __header__ is neither int nor float nor list/array thereof
>
>
> ovr_code = """
> functions{
> real revenue(real y, real B, real b) {
> real rev;
> rev <- if_else(y>b, y, b);
> rev <- if_else(B>y, 0, rev);
> return rev;
> }
> }

I'd code this as follows, but your tastes may vary:

if (B > y) return 0;
if (y > b) return y;
return b;

> data {
> int<lower=0> N; // number of observations
> int<lower=1> d; // number of dimensions
> matrix[N,d] x; // covariates
> vector[N] B; // highest bid
> vector[N] b; // second bid
> int<lower=0,upper=1> z[N]; // hallucinated data
> }
> parameters {
> real w0; // intercept
> vector[d] w; // weight vector
> real<lower=0> sigma; // std
> vector[N] y; // reserve price
>
> }
> model {
> y ~ normal(w0 + x*w, sigma);
> for (i in 1:N)
> z[i] ~ bernoulli(exp(-revenue(y[i],B[i],b[i])));
> }

I take it the inferential goal here is to estimate the reserve price
y and covariates w and w0.

Stan's going to potentially have problems with this model because
of the discontinuity in y due to the revenue() function not being
smooth.

Also, if you wanted to do a logistic regression rather than using
the non-stand link function, it'd be:

z[i] ~ bernoulli_logit(-revenue(y[i], B[i], b[i]));

You're also going to have to be careful that z[i] == 1 whenever
revenue(y[i], B[i], b[i]) = 0. So make sure it's a focused
hallucination!

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan: Value error in misc.py
parts:
Hi Allen and Bob,

Thanks for the quick reply!
The problem was indeed with the data dictionary. I was loading the dict using scipy.io.loadmat() from a mat file and the resulting dictionary had a '__header__' key. Deleting it and other key value pairs not used in the model solved the problem.

Further, I did change the bernoulli() to bernoulli_logit() as suggested. Bob, as you hinted the model is not suitable for sampling based methods because of the discontinuity and I get the error message
RuntimeError: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?

Does that mean I should give up using stan for this kind of model? (I have an EM algorithm running)

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] PyStan: Value error in misc.py
parts:
You have the same problems for EM, right? Did you marginalize
out the discontinuity there? If so, you can do the same
thing with Stan.

Stan shouldn't break --- it'll just devolve to a random walk
(like Metropolis). I'm guessing the problem is that you
are providing inits with 0 probability. Are you sure your
data is consistent with the likelihood?

- Bob
